newsitem.title: USA: GM UAW workers ok pact at Cadillac plant.
newsitem.headline: GM UAW workers ok pact at Cadillac plant.

text.p: Workers at General Motors Corp.'s Cadillac assembly plant here approved a new local labor contract by a 56 percent margin, despite a majority of skilled trades workers voting against the contract, union officials said Tuesday.
The contract calls for GM to hire a total of about 400 new workers at the plant, including 360 jobs the automaker agreed to add last spring.

Ed Patasznik, president of United Auto Workers Local 22, said the union will continue talks with GM to try to address the concerns of the skilled trades workers, but the new local pact will go into effect because it was approved by a majority of members who voted.
Union officials attributed the skilled trades rejections to certain provisions that allow GM to subcontract some work.
Local 22's 3,600 members had threatened to strike, but a deal in the early morning hours of August 9 averted a walkout. The plant assembles Cadillac's Seville, DeVille and El Dorado models.
Workers at two GM transmission plants in Ypsilanti and Romulus, Mich., which narrowly averted strikes on August 15, are scheduled to vote on their proposed contract on August 27.
GM shares were up 2-1/8 to 63-1/8 Tuesday.
